comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for a new restaurant with Type 41 beer-and-wine license at 276 5th St (51 m), MUR zoning within the same SoMa Youth and Family SUD. Change of use from vacant to restaurant, decided in November 2018.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This is the only decided CUA in the candidate pool and the only comparable requiring a Commission hearing. It was approved in 229 days (April to November 2018), demonstrating that restaurant uses with alcohol in the Youth and Family SUD are approvable through CUA. The concept does not serve alcohol, which shortens the path, but the SUD still triggers CUA for any restaurant use.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at the same 276 5th St address (51 m), MUR and Youth and Family SUD. Approved a limited restaurant in July 2018, three months before the CUA for the full restaurant with alcohol at the same site. Filed after the CUA was in process.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning noted 'On-site sale of alcohol requires CUA per SUD,' confirming that the Youth and Family SUD imposes CUA on alcohol service but not on dry restaurant uses. This concept serves no alcohol, so if the use is already established the change might be treated as continuation under Section 841 rather than a new CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health department referral for restaurant at 917 Folsom St (21 m next door), MUR zoning, approved March 2020 in 27 days. An agency referral approving continuation of restaurant use on the same block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referrals for continuation of existing restaurant use in MUR are approved quickly (under 30 days). However, this is an agency referral, not a use decision; it tells us the site next door has operated as a restaurant but says nothing about whether a CUA would be required or approved for a new change of use at 921 Folsom.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral at 917 Folsom (21 m), MUR zoning, approved August 2015. Transfer of Type 47 full-bar license for restaurant with catering, approved per Sections 841.45 and 841.81 as principally permitted.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Restaurant uses with alcohol licenses at 917 Folsom were approved as agency referrals (not CUAs) in 2015, before the Youth and Family SUD was mapped or before its rules were consistently applied. This suggests the immediate block has a multi-year track record of restaurant and alcohol use, but those approvals predate current SUD enforcement.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health referral at 915 Folsom (21 m), MUR, approved February 2018 in 6 days as 'permitted use / not a change of use under PC 841,' meaning continuation of existing restaurant.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Another continuation approval on the same block, processed as an agency referral in under a week. The record confirms the immediate Folsom Street frontage has multiple established restaurant uses, which may support a finding that this use is consistent with the existing character of the corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral for restaurant (DNA Pizza) at 917 Folsom (21 m), MUR, approved October 2015 in 7 days per Section 841.45.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Restaurant use at 917 Folsom approved as principally permitted in 2015. Multiple overlapping approvals at 915-917 Folsom show that site has cycled through several restaurant permits and operators, all approved without CUA hearings at that time.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health referral for new restaurant at 212 6th St (292 m), NCT-SOMA zoning, approved February 2020 in 52 days. Notes BPA approval and Section 311 neighborhood notice completed.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A new restaurant in a nearby neighborhood commercial district required a building permit alteration (BPA) with Section 311 notice but no CUA, because restaurants are principally permitted in NCT-SOMA. In contrast, the Youth and Family SUD at 921 Folsom imposes CUA even though MUR normally permits restaurants.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH referral for limited restaurant in MUR (address not shown but 107 m), approved October 2020 in 22 days as continuation of existing use per Section 841.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Continuation of limited restaurant use in MUR approved quickly as an agency referral. The speed suggests Planning treats Section 841 continuation cases as ministerial when the use is not abandoned, but a change from limited to full restaurant may not qualify as continuation.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline is 135–345 days and the cost is $5,200–$21,400 to obtain the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization, health permit to operate and building permit with change of use. These are the days to approval when the approvals are granted, not to a denial or withdrawal. The timeline counts from filing the CU application to final issuance of the health permit and building permit, which cannot occur until after the CU is approved and any appeal period expires. The one comparable CUA for a restaurant in the Youth and Family SUD took 229 days from filing to approval (April to November 2018); budget 4–8 months for CU review, hearing, adoption and appeal period, then 2–4 months for concurrent building permit and health permit plan check, inspections and final issuance. Costs: CU application fee ~$3,100 (2023 estimate); health plan check $828–$2,207; health permit to operate $470–$1,000; building permit $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation; sign permit $300–$1,500. The cost range reflects uncertainty in TI scope and valuation. State and federal registrations (EIN, seller's permit, entity formation, EDD, food safety certs, music licenses) add $570–$3,000 and 1–35 days but are not in the entitlement path. If the concept is part of a formula-retail chain and the Central SoMa SUD's formula-retail prohibition applies, the timeline and cost cannot be estimated because that overlay may prohibit the use outright; confirm at the pre-application meeting.

records_summary: 921 Folsom St is in the MUR zoning district within the SoMa Youth and Family Special Use District, which requires Conditional Use Authorization for any restaurant use. The records show no prior applications at this exact address or parcel. The immediate block is moderately active with four food/drink businesses within 500 ft and four active ABC licenses (one Type 47, one Type 41, two off-sale). Within 1,000 ft there are only two dated Planning decisions in the last 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate—but both were approved: one CUA for a restaurant with a Type 41 license at 276 5th St (229 days, approved 2018) and one agency referral for a limited restaurant continuation.
data_gaps: No hearing transcripts or staff reports extracted for the 276 5th St CUA, so the specific conditions and community concerns are unknown.
No records explain why the Youth and Family SUD was drawn to include this block or what the Commission's posture is toward new restaurant CUAs here.
The existing use at 921 Folsom is stated as 'limited restaurant' in the concept profile, but no DPH permit or Planning record confirms that use is active or grandfathered.
ABC does not publish conditions for the Type 47 and Type 41 licenses nearby, so undue-concentration or crime-district findings are not visible.
The two comparable decisions are too few and too varied (one CUA, one continuation referral) to predict timeline or conditions for a new restaurant CUA.
